Compute
Match — Reservation Request Lifecycle and Status Reference
This document explains, end to end, how a reservation request moves
through statuses, who triggers each change, and which timers apply.
Two levels of status
Reservation request status
— the status of the
whole customer request.
Offering status
— the status of each NCP’s slice
(
ReservationRequestOffering
). A request sent to 3 NCPs has
3 offerings.
Do not confuse these with
GPU offering status
(inventory listing status:
ACTIVE
,
PENDING_REVIEW
,
REJECTED
).

Catalog / multi-NCP flow,
step by step
Customer submits
(
POST /api/v1/reservation-request
). The backend creates the
request and the customer’s first proposal, then routes it: one offering
per selected cluster (backend limit 10, UI limit 3 by default).
Each offering starts as
AwaitingProviderAcceptance
with
acceptance_expiry_date = now + 7 days
. The request
becomes
AwaitingProviderAcceptance
.
Temporal starts a parent
ReservationRequestWorkflow
and
one child
OfferingLifecycleWorkflow
per offering. The
customer gets a “request received” email; each NCP gets a magic-link
email.
NCP accepts
→ offering
InProcess
,
contract_expiry_date = now + 45 days
, NCP and customer
receive an introduction email. The first acceptance moves the request to
InProcess
.
NCP counteroffers
→ a new proposal is recorded
(price-only changes update in place; material changes create a new
proposal in history).
NCP confirms contract
→ offering
Contracted
, an
Allocation
is created
(status
scheduled
), the request becomes
Contracted
, and sibling offerings are
Cancelled
with “superseded” emails.
NCP rejects
(remarks required) → offering
Rejected
. If all offerings are rejected, the request is
Rejected
.
Timers
: if an NCP does not accept in 7 days →
offering
Expired
. If no contract in 45 days → offering
Expired
. When every offering has expired, the customer
gets one consolidated expiry email and the request becomes
Expired
. Reminders go out 3 days before each
deadline.
Customer cancels
→ request
Cancelled
; NCPs are notified.
Extensions
: a Platform Admin (scope
accept_contract_extension
) can extend acceptance or
contract deadlines by 1–200 days; this can revive an Expired
offering.

Custom request flow
A custom request has no selected cluster
(
gpu_offering_id
is empty and there are no offerings).
Open ──▶ InReview ──▶ Matched
│
│──────▶ Unserviceable
│──────────────────▶ Matched / Unserviceable
└── customer cancel (from Open or InReview) ──▶ Cancelled
Only admins with
approver_manage_custom_reservation_request
move it
forward.
Only the customer cancels.
Never returns to Open; Matched, Unserviceable and Cancelled are
final.
Custom requests never expire.
Each transition records a timestamp and optional NCP name, NCP
region and comment, and emails the customer.
Capacity rules that affect
requests
Capacity windows of the same type (AVAILABLE or FUTURE) cannot
partially overlap; at most one open-ended window per type.
Availability checks use the
upper bound
of the
tenure band (for example
2-3
years is checked as 3 years)
to be conservative.
Allocations only subtract from the matching capacity type.
An optional cap
(
MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS_PER_REGIONAL_CAPACITY
, default 0 =
unlimited) hides clusters with too many pending requests and rejects new
requests against them.
GPU count per request must be between 1 and 100,000.
Contracted price must be zero or positive and is only visible to
NCPs and NVIDIA admins.
